verdict.rationale: The Agent Skills spec makes a `description` field required in every SKILL.md and says it should state both what the skill does and when to use it. The official template and the spec's PDF example follow that pattern, and frontmatter can control whether the user or Claude invokes a skill. However, activation is decided by the model when it judges a skill relevant, and the "when" part of the description is a "should", not an enforced rule. Several users report skills often aren't triggered as described (Vercel evals: never invoked in 56% of cases), so the description does not reliably predict behavior. Missing for 10: enforcement that every skill documents its activation conditions, deterministic or inspectable activation so behavior is predictable, independent evidence that the documented triggers match actual invocation.

support.subject: As a developer, every skill documents what it does and when it activates, so I can predict my agent's new behavior before it surprises me

citations.quote: The required `description` field: Must be 1-1024 characters, Should describe both what the skill does and when to use it
description: Replace with description of the skill and when Claude should use it.
If Claude thinks the skill is relevant to the current task, it will load the skill by reading its full `SKILL.md` into context.
